q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT T.CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER AS C INNER JOIN PRODUCT AS P ON C.PRODUCT_KEY=P.PRODUCT_KEY GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT C.PRODUCT_KEY)=(SELECT COUNT(1) FROM PRODUCT)) AS T

counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 selects customer IDs where the count of distinct products they have is equal to the total count of distinct products in the database. Q2 selects customer IDs where the count of distinct products they have is equal to the total count of products in the database, regardless of whether the products are distinct or not.
